release.label: Academy Atlas 0.1
release.truthBoundary: This is a designed portfolio and pricing hypothesis. It does not claim enrollment, institutional partnership, validated demand, or forty operating academies.

portfolio.thesis: Advance the thinking and making capacity of students, creators, experts, teams, and institutions through one portable Academy substrate.
portfolio.operatingModel: One control plane, five public houses, forty installable domain packs, learner-controlled exports, and replaceable community surfaces.
portfolio.brandPolicy: A domain pack may graduate into a standalone brand only after it proves a distinct buyer, promise, distribution loop, steward base, and risk boundary.
observed: Graph Engineering has a public source plugin, contract fixtures, and a read-only Observatory.
The existing portfolio already contains Starlight, GenCreator, Arcanea, and FrankX-facing surfaces.
Amsterdam and global institutions host technically and creatively adjacent learners; none are represented here as partners.
hypothesized: The forty domain packs cover a useful idea sweet spot.
The listed personas, modules, community formats, and prices will create demand.
Managed Ultra and institutional capacity can subsidize the open Commons.

openAccess.accessibilityRequirement: Every core path must have a low-bandwidth text route, captions or transcripts, keyboard access, and exportable artifacts.
openAccess.paidBoundary: Payment buys managed capacity, private tenancy, integrations, observability, group review availability, and service guarantees. It never buys hidden knowledge, a softer rubric, or a stronger credential.

commerce.execution: A deterministic payment adapter may execute only against a versioned human-ratified price book and explicit learner confirmation.
commerce.crossSubsidyHypothesis: Reserve 20% of Ultra and institutional contribution margin for Commons compute credits, accessibility work, and community stewardship; ratify quarterly before allocation.

requirements: A distinct learner problem is observed repeatedly.
The complete free route works without managed services.
At least two stewards other than the founder can facilitate the pack.
The pack passes accessibility, privacy, license, and human-authority review.

pricingTiers.label: Commons
pricingTiers.includes: All modules, missions, rubrics, local or BYOK execution, community reading and contribution, portable export, and equal credential eligibility.
pricingTiers.neverIncludes: Managed compute, private tenancy, service guarantees, or guaranteed review capacity.

pricingTiers.label: Managed Studio
pricingTiers.includes: Managed model routing, modest storage and compute, synced workspaces, and shared studio tooling.
pricingTiers.neverIncludes: One-to-one coaching, private assessment standards, or agent authority over consequential decisions.

pricingTiers.label: Agentic Workspace
pricingTiers.includes: Higher managed capacity, private project memory, sandbox runs, integrations, observability, and reusable agent workspaces.
pricingTiers.neverIncludes: Automatic publication, enrollment, pricing, payment, credential, or permission decisions.

pricingTiers.label: Guided Season
pricingTiers.includes: A small learning cell, scheduled group studios, peer critique, bounded human review windows, and managed capacity.
pricingTiers.neverIncludes: A founder retainer, private curriculum, or guaranteed commercial outcome.

pricingTiers.label: Ultra Managed
pricingTiers.includes: Private agentic workspace, substantial managed compute and storage, priority group review windows, advanced integrations, audit trails, and a small operator cell.
pricingTiers.neverIncludes: Standing one-to-one access, hidden knowledge, a softer rubric, or autonomous financial authority.

pricingTiers.label: Institution Department
pricingTiers.includes: Private tenancy, SSO and approved integrations, facilitator enablement, governance templates, observability, service guarantees, and Commons sponsorship.
pricingTiers.neverIncludes: Replacement of academic governance, automatic student decisions, or ownership of learner work.

tasks: Translate a learner-stated goal into two or three transparent pack options.
Show prerequisites, the complete free route, managed-capacity choices, assumptions, and source dates.
Stop before enrollment, payment, submission, publication, assessment, or credential action.
Compile sources, persona observations, modules, missions, community formats, and pricing hypotheses into a draft domain pack.
Mark sourced, derived, and hypothesized claims separately.
Return the draft to a named human owner for acceptance or rejection.
Prepare a bounded adoption map from an institution's existing curriculum and governance to Academy interfaces.
Identify local ownership, privacy, accessibility, integration, and facilitator requirements.
Stop before contracting, provisioning, migration, learner decisions, or external communication.

houses.name: Starlight Intelligence
houses.thesis: Design trustworthy human-and-agent systems that turn judgment into governed capability.
houses.communityFormat: Architecture guilds, open design reviews, repository missions, and human-authority clinics.

packs.name: Augmented Reasoning Architect
packs.promise: Design reasoning environments in which people and models make better decisions together.

persona.stage: advanced student or early-career solution designer
persona.interest: AI, interaction design, systems thinking, and human judgment
persona.currentReality: Builds prototypes or analyses inside a technical or design program
persona.friction: Has tool fluency but no coherent reasoning architecture or authority model

packs.academicExperience: A studio sequence joining cognitive task analysis, interface prototyping, evaluation, and human-authority design.
packs.communityExperience: Cross-disciplinary design cells critique one real decision environment each week.
packs.freeOutcome: A tested reasoning-environment prototype, decision record, and portable architecture map.
packs.managedCapacity: Private project memory, model routing, evaluation runs, and group architecture review.
packs.willingnessHypothesis: Likely to pay when managed evaluation and reusable project memory reduce prototype setup time.

packs.name: Agentic Systems Architect
packs.promise: Compile bounded agent workflows with explicit memory, tools, recovery, and human decision rights.

persona.stage: software engineer, AI product lead, or technical founder
persona.interest: agents, workflows, reliability, and product architecture
persona.currentReality: Can build model-powered features and now faces orchestration complexity
persona.friction: Demos work, but authority, failure recovery, and observability remain implicit

packs.academicExperience: Contract-first systems work across task decomposition, tool policies, memory boundaries, evals, and runtime observability.
packs.communityExperience: Architecture reviews pair builders with adversarial failure-mode reviewers.
packs.freeOutcome: A locally runnable agent workflow, contract, eval set, and failure receipt.
packs.managedCapacity: Hosted sandboxes, traces, model routing, integration adapters, and shared reliability clinics.
packs.willingnessHypothesis: Experienced builders may pay for reproducible sandboxes, trace retention, and bounded review capacity.

packs.name: Capability Graph Architect
packs.promise: Turn a role or practice into capabilities, missions, artifacts, evaluators, and learner-controlled proof.

persona.stage: solution designer, learning designer, engineering lead, or academy builder
persona.interest: graphs, curriculum architecture, competence, and open learning
persona.currentReality: Owns a role, curriculum, repository, or expert method that is hard to teach coherently
persona.friction: Content exists, but capabilities, execution, assessment, and authority are disconnected

packs.academicExperience: A public Mission Zero and capability-to-artifact path backed by machine-readable Academy contracts.
packs.communityExperience: Open graph reviews, mission defenses, and contributor stewardship around a shared source plugin.
packs.freeOutcome: A versioned capability graph, one executable mission, validation receipt, and public-source contribution path.
packs.managedCapacity: Optional hosted graph workbench, private repository connectors, and group review availability.
packs.willingnessHypothesis: Current source work proves inspectability, not demand; paid capacity must be tested separately.

packs.name: Context and Memory Engineer
packs.promise: Build purpose-bound memory and retrieval systems that preserve provenance, privacy, and useful continuity.

persona.stage: AI engineer, knowledge engineer, or computational-media student
persona.interest: context engineering, retrieval, memory, and personal intelligence
persona.currentReality: Experiments with RAG or model memory across projects
persona.friction: Context is copied everywhere, provenance decays, and private boundaries blur

packs.academicExperience: Hands-on work across information architecture, retrieval evaluation, temporal context, consent, and data minimization.
packs.communityExperience: Redacted dataset clinics and retrieval-debugging circles around locally runnable systems.
packs.freeOutcome: A local memory prototype, retrieval eval, deletion path, and provenance report.
packs.managedCapacity: Encrypted managed storage, connectors, scheduled evaluations, and observability.
packs.willingnessHypothesis: Builders may pay for secure connectors and managed evaluations while retaining export and deletion rights.

packs.name: Human Authority Designer
packs.promise: Make consequential decisions, appeals, escalation, and responsibility legible inside AI-enabled systems.

persona.stage: service designer, policy professional, product owner, or responsible-AI lead
persona.interest: governance, service design, ethics, and institutional AI
persona.currentReality: Reviews or designs systems that affect people
persona.friction: Human oversight exists as a slogan rather than a timed, owned, testable control

packs.academicExperience: Case-based design across authority mapping, appeals, consent, accessibility, red-team scenarios, and service operations.
packs.communityExperience: Authority clinics bring designers, technologists, and domain stewards to one consequential workflow.
packs.freeOutcome: A human-authority map, tested escalation protocol, and appeal-ready service blueprint.
packs.managedCapacity: Private scenario workspaces, audit trails, policy connectors, and facilitated group reviews.
packs.willingnessHypothesis: Teams may fund a bounded season when governance must become operational before deployment.

packs.name: AI Product Prototyper
packs.promise: Move from a real user decision to a testable AI product without hiding uncertainty or overbuilding infrastructure.

persona.stage: design, computing, or entrepreneurship student and early product builder
persona.interest: AI products, interaction, rapid making, and user research
persona.currentReality: Can prompt and assemble prototypes but lacks product evidence
persona.friction: Builds model demos before identifying the user moment, authority boundary, or evaluation condition

packs.academicExperience: A make-test-decide studio across user research, model behavior, interface states, evaluation, and deployment constraints.
packs.communityExperience: Weekly prototype tables with users, designers, and technical peers.
packs.freeOutcome: A tested prototype, evaluation set, user-research notes, and release decision.
packs.managedCapacity: Hosted prototypes, model routing, analytics, sandboxes, and shared user-testing operations.
packs.willingnessHypothesis: Students and early builders may pay a modest fee for hosted prototypes and repeatable test infrastructure.

packs.name: Evaluation and Safety Designer
packs.promise: Define what good, unsafe, uncertain, and human-only mean before an AI system earns trust.

persona.stage: researcher, QA lead, AI engineer, or policy-minded product professional
persona.interest: evals, safety, measurement, and responsible release
persona.currentReality: Owns quality for a model-powered feature or research prototype
persona.friction: Metrics are abundant but decision relevance, holdouts, and human adjudication are weak

packs.academicExperience: Evaluation design across claim boundaries, datasets, adversarial cases, human assessment, and release gates.
packs.communityExperience: Blind evaluation exchanges and failure-review circles use redacted, inspectable artifacts.
packs.freeOutcome: An evaluation contract, benchmark set, human adjudication guide, and release receipt.
packs.managedCapacity: Scheduled eval runs, secure holdouts, trace analysis, and shared review operations.
packs.willingnessHypothesis: Professional teams may pay for secure, repeatable evaluation operations rather than proprietary knowledge.

packs.name: Intelligence Operations Lead
packs.promise: Run a governed portfolio of human-and-agent workflows as an observable operating system for a team.

persona.stage: operations leader, innovation lead, chief of staff, or transformation owner
persona.interest: AI adoption, operations, governance, and organizational learning
persona.currentReality: Coordinates multiple pilots, tools, and teams
persona.friction: Local wins do not compound into shared capability, ownership, or reliable operating rhythms

packs.academicExperience: Operating-system design across portfolio mapping, workflow contracts, measurement, governance, and facilitator practice.
packs.communityExperience: Private operator councils exchange redacted patterns and publish reusable Commons methods.
packs.freeOutcome: An operating map, one governed workflow, adoption scorecard, and reusable facilitation kit.
packs.managedCapacity: Private tenancy, integrations, observability, service guarantees, and facilitator enablement.
packs.willingnessHypothesis: Departments may pay when the substrate consolidates fragmented pilots without replacing local governance.
